evaluation.overall_assessment: This page is evaluated against WCAG 2.2.2 (Pause, Stop, Hide), which is the primary applicable criterion here. The page contains auto-updating content (a random number in a <span id='target'>) that is controlled by a JavaScript function started via the body's onload attribute. Critically, a button with id='control' and value='Pause changes' is provided, which calls toggleUpdates() to allow the user to pause the auto-updating content — satisfying the requirement of WCAG 2.2.2 that moving, blinking, scrolling, or auto-updating information can be paused, stopped, or hidden. For WCAG 1.3.5 (Identify Input Purpose), the only interactive element is a button, which is not a data-collection input field that requires autocomplete attributes, making this criterion inapplicable. For WCAG 1.4.3 (Contrast Minimum), no inline styles or color declarations are present in the HTML, so default browser colors apply and no contrast failure can be identified from the source alone; the criterion is effectively passed by absence of overriding styles. For WCAG 1.4.12 (Text Spacing), no CSS is defined that would restrict text spacing overrides, so the criterion passes. For WCAG 2.4.8 (Location), this is a single standalone page with no site navigation or breadcrumb context required, making the criterion inapplicable. Overall, the page passes all applicable criteria, most notably 2.2.2 by providing a clearly labeled pause control for the auto-updating content.

issues.description: The <object> element embedding a PNG image uses aria-labelledby to reference a visible text label, which is a valid WCAG technique (ARIA10). However, the NVDA audit's static rule engine flagged it under 'alt_object' because it lacks a traditional fallback text alternative (e.g., a title attribute or inner text content). While aria-labelledby is a recognized mechanism, the <object> element has no inner fallback content and no title attribute, creating a risk that assistive technologies which do not fully support aria-labelledby on <object> elements will fail to announce the label.
issues.evidence: <object aria-labelledby="label" data="/WAI/content-assets/wcag-act-rules/test-assets/shared/w3c-logo.png"></object> — flagged by alt_object rule; aria_label: null, alt_attr: null, nvda_announcement: null (NVDA could not confirm announcement)
issues.recommendation: Supplement aria-labelledby with a title attribute (title="W3C logo") and/or include fallback inner text content inside the <object> element (e.g., <object ...>W3C logo</object>) to ensure broad assistive technology support. This satisfies WCAG Technique H53 alongside ARIA10.

issues.description: The page has no heading structure whatsoever (no <h1>–<h6> elements). While this minimal page may not strictly require headings, the absence of any structural semantics — combined with no landmarks (no <main>, <nav>, <header>, <footer>) — means relationships and structure are not conveyed programmatically.

issues.recommendation: Wrap the page content in a <main> landmark element to convey the primary content region. If the page grows to include multiple sections, add appropriate heading levels (starting with <h1>) to communicate structure programmatically.

issues.description: No skip navigation mechanism is present (no skip link, no landmark regions). While the page is currently minimal, the absence of a <main> landmark means there is no programmatic way to bypass any repeated blocks should the page be part of a larger site.
issues.evidence: run_nvda_full_audit wcag_2_4_1: skip_links_found=[], has_skip_link=false, landmarks={main:0, nav:0, header:0, footer:0}. Verdict returned N/A only because no repeated nav blocks were detected — but no bypass mechanism exists.
issues.recommendation:
Add a
landmark to wrap the primary content. If this page is part of a site with repeated navigation, add a skip link as the first focusable element (e.g., Skip to main content).

evaluation.overall_assessment: The page fails primarily on WCAG 1.1.1 (Non-text Content): the <object> element embedding a W3C logo PNG uses aria-labelledby to reference a visible text label, which is a recognized technique (ARIA10), but NVDA was unable to confirm the announcement (nvda_announcement: null), and the element lacks any fallback inner text or title attribute — creating a real-world risk that some assistive technologies will not expose the label. Additionally, the page lacks any landmark regions or heading structure, raising concerns under WCAG 1.3.1 (Info and Relationships) and WCAG 2.4.1 (Bypass Blocks). WCAG 2.1.1 (Keyboard) and 4.1.2 (Name, Role, Value) are inapplicable as there are no interactive elements. The most critical fix is to add robust fallback text inside the <object> element and supplement with a title attribute, alongside wrapping content in a <main> landmark.

Use a <span> with descriptive text and link it via aria-describedby. Mark required fields with a visible asterisk (*) and a legend explaining 'Fields marked with * are required', plus add aria-required='true' to those inputs.

issues.evidence:
The page has no breadcrumb navigation, no site navigation landmark, and no indication of where this registration page sits within a larger site structure. There is only a single

Register

with no surrounding context.
